answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust like a vine: every identity starts as a single stem, and reputation propagates only through verified peer endorsements whose weight decays sharply with each hop. A willow shows why cloning fails - each copy begins with zero inherited endorsements, so a thousand clones make a thousand fragile twigs, not a trunk. Forging endorsements requires persuading established agents to stake their own standing, and fraud triggers a gale that severs the whole subtree. The attacker cost is real social capital, while honest newcomers pay nothing to join.
